topic_title: Pronoun in English Grammar – SBI PO Level Error Detection

intro_payload.title: Pronoun Mastery: SBI PO Level Error Detection
learning_outcomes: Master all 9 types of Pronouns from zero level to Officer level
Crack Case Errors (I/me, he/him, who/whom) like SBI PO toppers
Decode Reflexive, Reciprocal & Demonstrative Pronoun exceptions
Handle Ambiguous Reference & Dummy 'It' errors confidently
Practice 36+ SBI PO style Error Detection questions

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ek sentence bol - 'Sita ne Sita ki kitab Sita ke bag mein rakhi.' Kaisa lag raha hai sunne mein?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir bahut ajeeb lag raha hai, baar baar 'Sita' aa raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda! Isiliye hum bolte hain - 'Sita ne apni kitab apne bag mein rakhi.' Yahan 'apni/apne' ne 'Sita' ki jagah le li.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh ye jo naam ki jagah wala word aaya, wahi kuch special cheez hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi, Raju. Us word ko English grammar mein 'PRONOUN' kehte hain. Definition yaad rakho: 'A Pronoun is a word used INSTEAD OF a Noun, to avoid its repetition.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh he, she, it, they - ye sab pronoun hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! I, we, you, he, she, it, they, this, that, who, which - ye sab noun ki jagah use hote hain. Naam bhool jao, kaam yaad rakho - 'noun ki jagah lena'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Samajh gaya sir, matlab pronoun ek 'substitute player' hai noun ke liye, cricket team jaisa!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab ek zaroori cheez suno - jis original noun (Sita) ki jagah pronoun (apni) aaya, use grammar mein 'ANTECEDENT' kehte hain. Antecedent matlab 'jispehle aaya' - wo noun jisse pronoun ka connection hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye 'Antecedent' word toh exam mein bahut hard lag raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ghabrao mat! Ye sirf ek naam hai concept ka - 'Antecedent' = original noun. BPSC aur SBI PO dono mein pronoun ka apne Antecedent se match hona (number, gender, person mein) sabse bada testing point hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Match hona? Matlab agar Antecedent singular hai toh pronoun bhi singular hona chahiye?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly, isi pe pura chapter khada hai! Ab sun lo Pronoun ke 9 types jo hum pura chapter mein cover karenge: Personal, Possessive, Reflexive, Intensive, Demonstrative, Interrogative, Relative, Indefinite, aur Reciprocal.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Itne saare?? Sir ye sab yaad kaise rahenge, mix ho jayenge!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tension mat lo, hum ek-ek karke, daily life examples se, step by step seekhenge. Har type ke baad SBI PO level error-detection practice bhi karenge.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Chalo sir, start karte hain - sabse pehla type kaunsa?

quiz_payload.question: A Pronoun is best defined as:

options.text: A word that describes a noun
A word used instead of a noun to avoid repetition
A word that joins two sentences

quiz_payload.explanation: Pronoun ki core definition yahi hai - noun ki jagah use hokar uski repetition avoid karna. Option A adjective ka kaam hai, C conjunction ka, D verb ka.

quiz_payload.question: In the sentence 'Ravi lost his bag', what is the Antecedent of the pronoun 'his'?
quiz_payload.explanation: Antecedent wo noun hai jiski jagah/reference mein pronoun use hota hai. Yahan 'his' Ravi ko refer kar raha hai, isliye Antecedent = Ravi.

quiz_payload.question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized type of Pronoun in English Grammar?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Descriptive Pronoun' koi standard grammar category nahi hai - ye trap option hai. Standard types: Personal, Possessive, Reflexive, Intensive, Demonstrative, Interrogative, Relative, Indefinite, Reciprocal.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Foundation strong hai toh officer banna pakka hai! Chalo ab Personal Pronoun ke case system mein ghuste hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, sochte hain school mein attendance ho rahi hai. Teacher poochti hai 'Who did this?' Tum jawab doge 'I did it' ya 'Me did it'?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'I did it' bolenge, 'Me did it' toh galat lagta hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Perfect! Jab pronoun sentence ka SUBJECT (jo kaam kar raha hai) hota hai, tab I, we, you, he, she, it, they use hote hain - ye 'Subjective Case' kehlata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh subject wale pronoun hamesha sentence ke shuru mein hi aayenge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Mostly haan, lekin asli test hai jab pronoun sentence ka OBJECT banta hai - matlab jispe kaam ho raha hai. Jaise 'Teacher scolded me' - yahan 'me' hai, 'I' nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh me, us, you, him, her, it, them - ye sab OBJECT wale pronoun hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Isse 'Objective Case' kehte hain. Ye tab use hote hain jab pronoun kisi verb ka object ho ya kisi preposition (to, for, with, at, from) ke baad aaye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye preposition wala part thoda confusing lag raha hai, example doge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Zaroor, ruko pehle ek aur important cheez sun lo. 'This is my book' aur 'This book is mine' - dono mein possession dikha rahe hain, but 'my' aur 'mine' mein farak hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir dono ka matlab toh same hai - kitab meri hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Matlab same hai, but 'my' ke baad hamesha noun aayega (my book), isliye ye Possessive ADJECTIVE hai. 'Mine' akela khada hoke pura noun replace karta hai (This book is mine), isliye ye Possessive PRONOUN hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohhh! Toh 'my/his/her/our/their' adjective hain aur 'mine/his/hers/ours/theirs' pronoun hain? SBI PO mein ye mix karke poochenge kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul poochenge, isliye yahi golden rule gaanth baandh lo: PREPOSITION (to, for, with, between, of, at) ke turant baad hamesha OBJECTIVE case aayega - never Subjective.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'between you and I' galat hoga? Ye toh log bolte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda tumne SBI PO ka sabse famous trap! 'Between' ek preposition hai, isliye correct hoga 'between you and ME'. 'Between you and I' 90% logo ki galti hai but exam mein error hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Ye toh mummy bhi bolti hain aise, ab pata chala galat hai!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Him and his brother / (B) are going to the market / (C) to buy some vegetables / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Him and his brother' subject hai sentence ka (going action kar raha hai), isliye Subjective case 'He' aayega, na ki Objective 'Him'. Correct: 'He and his brother are going...'

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) This matter is / (B) strictly confidential / (C) between you and I / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Between' ek preposition hai, uske baad Objective case aana chahiye. Correct: 'between you and me'. 'Between you and I' classic SBI PO/high-level trap hai.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) This house is / (B) more bigger than / (C) her's / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Possessive Pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) mein KABHI apostrophe (') nahi lagta. 'Her's' galat hai, correct hoga 'hers'. (Bonus trap: 'more bigger' bhi galat hai but yahan bade error 'her's' ko highlight kiya gaya hai as per SBI PO pattern of picking the clearest violation).

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Case system clear ho gaya! Ab hum case ke aur bhi khatarnak traps dekhenge - comparison wale sentences.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, 'Ram is taller than I' aur 'Ram is taller than me' - dono mein se kaunsa sahi hai?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir mujhe toh 'than me' zyada natural lagta hai bolne mein.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Natural lagta hai, but grammar rule kehta hai - 'than' aur 'as' ke baad wo case use hoga jo poora sentence complete karne pe sahi baithe. Yahan poora sentence hai 'Ram is taller than I AM (tall)' - isliye 'I' sahi hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab hidden verb sochni padegi 'than/as' ke baad? Ye toh naya trick hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Aur ye 'I/me' confusion ki wajah se logo ne ek galat aadat bana li hai jise 'Hypercorrection' kehte hain - hamesha 'I' use karna sochke ki wo zyada polite/correct lagta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab jaise humne pichhle card mein 'between you and I' dekha tha?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly wahi! Log sochte hain 'me' bolna galat/rude hai isliye har jagah 'I' thok dete hain - 'He gave the book to Ram and I' - ye bhi galat hai kyunki 'to' preposition hai, 'me' aayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh trick ye hai - sentence ko chota karke check karo ki akela 'I' ya 'me' theek lagta hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi trick pakdi tumne! Ye 'shortening trick' SBI PO mein bahut kaam aati hai. 'Ram and (I/me) went to the market' - kaunsa sahi hoga?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ise chota karke check karta hoon - '(I/me) went to market' - toh 'I went' sahi lagta hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Perfect application! Toh correct hoga 'Ram and I went to the market'. Yahi trick 'him and me/he and I' jaise compound subjects aur objects mein hamesha use karo.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wah sir, ye toh ek hi trick se saare compound pronoun errors solve ho jayenge!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aakhri twist. Formal/grammatical rule kehta hai: 'It is I' sahi hai kyunki 'is' ek Linking Verb hai, aur linking verb ke baad Subjective case aata hai, Objective nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Par sir 'It's me' toh sab bolte hain, phone pe bhi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi observe kiya - 'It's me' spoken/informal English mein widely accepted hai, but competitive exams mein FORMAL rule follow hota hai: 'It was he who called' - not 'It was him who called'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Samajh gaya sir, exam mein formal rule, ghar pe jo marzi bolo!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) My sister is / (B) much more intelligent / (C) than me / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Hidden verb trick lagao: '...than I (am)'. Poora sentence 'than I am intelligent' banega, isliye Subjective 'I' sahi hai, 'me' nahi. Correct: 'than I'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The manager gave / (B) the appraisal letters / (C) to Ravi and I / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'To' preposition hai, uske baad Objective case aayega. Shortening trick: 'gave the letters to (I/me)' - 'to me' sahi hai. Correct: 'to Ravi and me'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) When the phone rang / (B) everyone thought / (C) it was him who had called / (D) No error

options.text: it was him who had called

quiz_payload.explanation: Linking verb 'was' ke baad Subjective case aayega as per formal rule. Correct: 'it was he who had called'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Case traps ab tumse dar ke bhagenge! Agla module hai sabse zyada exam mein aane wala - Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, apartment ka guard bolta hai 'Sab resident apna apna gate pass dikhaye' - ek resident ke liye ya sab ke liye?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sab ke liye sir, isiliye 'apna apna' bola.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Yahi hai Agreement ka rule - Pronoun apne Antecedent ke NUMBER (singular/plural) aur GENDER (male/female) se match hona chahiye. 'The girl lost HER bag' - singular, feminine match ho raha hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'The boys lost their bags' bhi isi rule se sahi hai? Plural se plural match ho raha hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab BPSC ka favorite trap suno - Collective Nouns jaise 'team', 'jury', 'family', 'committee'. Ye ek group hain, ekta mein hain toh SINGULAR pronoun (it/its) lete hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'The team celebrated ITS victory' sahi hoga, na ki 'their victory'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Perfect! Lekin twist - agar team ke members alag-alag kaam kar rahe hain (disunity dikhani hai), tab PLURAL pronoun bhi chalta hai: 'The jury gave THEIR individual opinions'. Yeh exception professors ka favorite hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Same word 'team/jury' kabhi singular kabhi plural? Ye toh confusing hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aur zaroori rule: Jab do subjects 'AND' se juden ho, toh pronoun PLURAL aayega - 'Ram and Shyam finished THEIR work'. Lekin jab 'OR/NOR' se jude ho, toh pronoun sabse NAZDEEK wale subject se match karega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'Either Ram or the girls have lost THEIR bags' - yahan 'girls' pass hai isliye 'their'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi! Aur agar order palat de - 'Either the girls or Ram has lost HIS bag' - ab 'Ram' pass hai toh singular 'his' aayega. Ye 'Proximity Rule' kehlata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wah! Toh 'or/nor' mein last wale subject ko dekho, 'and' mein hamesha plural - yaad rakh liya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab sabse bada SBI PO/BPSC trap suno - 'Everyone', 'Everybody', 'Someone', 'Each' - ye sab grammatically SINGULAR maane jaate hain, chahe matlab 'sabka' ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'Everyone must submit their assignment' galat hai kya? Ye toh main hamesha bolta hoon!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Formal/exam grammar mein haan, ye galat maana jaata hai. Correct hoga - 'Everyone must submit HIS OR HER assignment' ya simply 'HIS assignment' (traditional rule). 'Their' ko modern spoken English mein accept karte hain, but exams mein 'his/her' expect karte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa, matlab 'everyone/each/everybody' dikhe toh dimaag mein singular pronoun bajna chahiye - alarm bell jaisa!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The committee has / (B) submitted their / (C) final report to the board / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Committee' ek unified action (submitted one report) kar raha hai, isliye Collective Noun singular treat hoga. Correct: 'submitted its final report'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Every student / (B) must bring / (C) their own laptop tomorrow / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Every student' singular hai, isliye pronoun bhi singular aayega. Correct: 'his or her own laptop' / 'his own laptop' (traditional exam rule).

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Neither the teacher nor the students / (B) have submitted / (C) his report yet / (D) No error

options.text: Neither the teacher nor the students

quiz_payload.explanation: Proximity Rule ke hisaab se, 'nor' ke baad nazdeek wala subject 'students' (plural) hai, isliye pronoun bhi plural aayega. Correct: 'their reports yet'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Ye sabse important module tha - clear kar liya! Ab chalte hain Reflexive aur Intensive Pronoun ki duniya mein.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, cycle chalate waqt tum gir gaye aur khud ko hi chot lagi - is situation ko English mein kaise bologe? 'I hurt me' ya kuch aur?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'I hurt me' bol sakte hain kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Nahi, jab action wapas subject pe hi aata hai (khud ko), tab 'self/selves' wale special pronoun use hote hain: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Correct: 'I hurt MYSELF'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh ye 'self' wale pronoun 'khud' ke liye hain - is liye inhe 'Reflexive' kehte honge, jaise mirror mein reflection?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Wah, mirror wala analogy bilkul sahi hai! Golden Rule: Reflexive pronoun tabhi use hoga jab Subject aur Object DONO SAME PERSON ho. 'He cut himself' - He hi kaat raha hai, He hi kat raha hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'He cut him' galat hoga kya sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'He cut him' ka matlab badal jaata hai - 'usne kisi doosre ko kaata'. Jabki 'He cut himself' ka matlab hai 'usne khud ko kaata'. Grammar mein dono ALAG meanings hain - dhyan se!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh, matlab meaning hi badal jayega agar 'himself' ki jagah 'him' likh diya toh? Bahut risky point hai ye!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab sabse bada SBI PO trap - office/corporate emails mein log galti se bolte hain 'Please contact Ravi or myself for details'. Kya ye sahi hai?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir lagta toh polite hai sunne mein!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Polite lagta hai but WRONG hai! 'Myself' sirf tab use hoga jab 'I' pehle se sentence mein subject ki तरह maujood ho, jaise 'I hurt myself'. Yahan koi 'I' subject nahi hai, isliye correct hoga 'Please contact Ravi or ME'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Seriously?? Ye toh mere office wale bhaiya bhi galat bolte hain phir! 'Myself Raju' bolna bhi galat hoga kya, jaise interview mein bolte hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda! 'Myself Raju' Indian English ki galti hai, correct hoga 'I am Raju' ya 'Myself, Raju' informal introduction mein. Ab suno same 'self' words ka doosra use bhi hota hai - EMPHASIS ke liye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab sir, jaise zor dene ke liye?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! 'The Principal HIMSELF gave the prize' - yahan 'himself' emphasis de raha hai ki khud Principal ne diya, na ki koi assistant. Ise 'Intensive Pronoun' kehte hain. Trick: Ise sentence se hata do, meaning wahi rahega, sirf emphasis kam ho jayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh Reflexive hata nahi sakte (meaning badal jayega), but Intensive hata sakte hain (sirf zor kam hoga)? Ye toh smart difference hai!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The manager requested / (B) Rina and myself / (C) to complete the project by Friday / (D) No error

options.text: to complete the project by Friday

quiz_payload.explanation: Reflexive pronoun 'myself' tabhi chalega jab 'I' subject roop mein pehle se maujood ho. Yahan subject 'The manager' hai, 'I' nahi. Correct: 'Rina and me'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) She always blames / (B) her for every / (C) small mistake she makes / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Subject 'She' aur Object dono same person hain (khud ko blame kar rahi hai), isliye Reflexive pronoun aayega. Correct: 'blames herself for every'.

quiz_payload.question: Identify the function of 'himself' in: 'The Principal himself distributed the prizes.'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Himself' yahan sirf emphasis de raha hai ki khud Principal ne prizes diye, koi object 'distribute' nahi ho raha khud pe. Isliye ye Intensive Pronoun hai, Reflexive nahi.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Corporate email trap crack kar liya! Ab dekhte hain do logo ke beech wale special pronouns - Reciprocal.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, tum aur tumhara best friend ek doosre ko birthday gift dete ho - 'We give gifts to ___ ' - kya word aayega?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'each other' bolte hain shayad?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Jab do ya zyada log ek MUTUAL action kar rahe ho (ek doosre pe), tab RECIPROCAL Pronoun use hota hai: 'each other' aur 'one another'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir dono ka matlab toh same hai, inme farak kya hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Traditional grammar rule (jo BPSC/SSC officer level pe poocha jata hai): 'EACH OTHER' use hota hai jab sirf DO (2) persons/things ke beech action ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'Ram and Shyam help each other' sahi hai, kyunki dono hi hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye sabse common example hai. Do dosto, do bhai-behen, husband-wife - jahan bhi sankhya '2' hai, wahan 'each other'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh agar teen ya usse zyada log ho toh?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tab hum use karte hain 'ONE ANOTHER' - jab TWO SE ZYADA (more than two) persons ke beech mutual action ho. Jaise 'All the students of the class help ONE ANOTHER'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir yaad rakhne ka koi tarika hai? 'Each' aur 'One' mein confuse ho jaunga!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Simple trick: 'EACH' sunte hi 'do haath' (dono taraf) imagine karo - 2 logo ka hi kaam hai. Aur 'ONE ANOTHER' mein socho 'ek se doosra, doosre se teesra' - chain jaisi, jo group mein chalti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wah! Ab clear hai - competitive exam mein ye bahut strictly follow karte honge?

guess_payload.question: Raju ko ek sentence mila: 'The five friends often visit ___ houses during Diwali.' Kaunsa correct hoga - guess karo!
guess_payload.explanation: 'Five friends' matlab do se zyada log hain, isliye 'one another's' sahi hoga (possessive form). Note: Dono reciprocal pronouns ka possessive form banta hai apostrophe-s lagakar - 'each other's' / 'one another's', jaise normal noun mein banta hai.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The two neighbouring countries / (B) have been fighting / (C) with one another for decades / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Two countries' matlab sirf DO parties hain, isliye 'each other' aayega, na ki 'one another' (jo do se zyada ke liye hai). Correct: 'with each other for decades'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) All the ten members of the club / (B) respect and / (C) trust each other completely / (D) No error

options.text: All the ten members of the club

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Ten members' matlab do se zyada log hain, isliye 'one another' use hoga (strictly), na ki 'each other'. Correct: 'trust one another completely'.

quiz_payload.question: Choose the correctly formed possessive Reciprocal Pronoun sentence:

options.text: The two sisters borrowed each others clothes.
The two sisters borrowed each other clothes.
The two sisters borrowed each other's clothes.
The two sisters borrowed each other' clothes.

quiz_payload.explanation: Reciprocal pronoun ka possessive form apostrophe + s se banta hai - 'each other's'. Option A mein apostrophe missing hai, D mein galat position pe hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Each other vs One another - ab kabhi confuse nahi hoge! Aage chalte hain 'this/that' wale Demonstrative Pronouns ki taraf.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, dukaan pe khada hoke ungli se dikhate hue bolo - 'ye wala' aur 'wo wala' - English mein kya bologe?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'this one' aur 'that one'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! This, That, These, Those - ye words kisi specific cheez ko POINT OUT (dikhana) karte hain, isliye inhe DEMONSTRATIVE Pronoun kehte hain - 'Demonstrate' matlab dikhana.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'this/that' paas-door ke liye hain aur 'these/those' bhi kuch aisa hi hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi socha! Do rules ek saath yaad rakho: DISTANCE (paas/door) aur NUMBER (singular/plural). This=paas+singular, That=door+singular, These=paas+plural, Those=door+plural.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'This are my books' galat hoga kya, kyunki 'books' plural hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul galat! 'This' singular hai, 'books' plural - number match nahi ho raha. Correct: 'These are my books'. Ye exam mein bahut common error hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, toh distance ke saath saath number bhi check karna padega, do cheezein ek saath dekhni hongi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek subtle point suno - 'This is my pen' mein 'this' Pronoun hai (akela khada hai, noun ki jagah). Lekin 'This pen is mine' mein 'this' ke baad 'pen' noun aa gaya - ab ye Demonstrative ADJECTIVE ban gaya, Pronoun nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir yahi toh possessive wale case mein bhi dekha tha - akela khade toh pronoun, noun ke saath toh adjective!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi connection banaya tumne! Yehi pattern hai - jab bhi koi word akele khada hoke noun replace kare, wo Pronoun hai; jab word ke baad noun aaye aur uski quality/pointer bataye, wo Adjective hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh exam mein 'This/That book' dikhega toh wo adjective hai, akela 'This/That' dikhega toh pronoun?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab ek high-level SBI PO trap - 'this kind of' aur 'these kind of' mein se kaunsa sahi hai?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir mujhe toh 'these kind of' hi sahi lagta hai kyunki aage plural noun aata hai jaise 'these kind of books'.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yehi sabse bada trap hai! Rule kehta hai - 'this/that' hamesha 'KIND/SORT/TYPE' (singular word) se match karega, 'books' se nahi. Correct: 'THIS kind of books' ya better 'THESE kinds of books'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Matlab 'kind' ke singular hone se match karna hai, jo aage noun hai usse nahi? Ye toh dimaag ghuma diya sir!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The problems in / (B) this chapter are much / (C) tougher than those in the last one / (D) No error

options.text: tougher than those in the last one

quiz_payload.explanation: No Error - 'this chapter' singular hai (correct), aur 'those' plural pronoun 'problems' ko refer karke correctly compare kar raha hai. Sentence structurally aur grammatically sahi hai.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) I have never seen / (B) these kind of / (C) mangoes anywhere else / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'This/That' ko 'kind/sort/type' (singular word) ke saath match karna hai, na ki aage aane wale plural noun se. Correct: 'this kind of'.

quiz_payload.question: In the sentence 'That is a beautiful painting', what is the grammatical function of 'That'?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'That' akela khada hai (no noun follows it directly), aur pura sentence ka subject bana raha hai - isliye ye Demonstrative Pronoun hai, na ki Adjective (jo 'that painting' jaisa hota).

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: 'This kind of' trap ab tumhe fasa nahi sakta! Ab chalo sawaal poochne wale Interrogative Pronouns ki taraf.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, dukaan pe koi cheez toot gayi aur mummy poochti hain - 'Ye kisne kiya?' English mein kya bologe?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'Who did this?'

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Who, Whom, Whose, Which, What - jab ye words SAWAAL (question) poochne ke liye use hote hain, tab inhe INTERROGATIVE Pronoun kehte hain. 'Interrogate' matlab poochtaachh karna.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'who' aur 'whom' dono hi 'kaun' ke liye lagte hain, inme farak kaise pata karein?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahi sabse bada exam-favorite topic hai! Simple rule: 'WHO' Subjective case hai (kaam karne wale ke liye), 'WHOM' Objective case hai (jispe kaam ho raha hai ya preposition ke baad).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir example se samjhao na, confuse ho raha hoon!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'WHO called you?' - yahan 'who' subject hai (call karne wala). 'WHOM did you call?' - yahan 'whom' object hai (jisse call kiya gaya). Trick: sentence ko jawab do 'he/him' se - agar 'he' fit ho toh 'who', agar 'him' fit ho toh 'whom'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! 'He called' - toh who sahi. 'You called him' - toh whom sahi. Wah, ye trick toh mast hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab ek aur trap - 'WHOSE' ka use hota hai POSSESSION (kiska/kiski) dikhane ke liye - 'WHOSE bag is this?' matlab 'ye bag kiska hai?'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir spelling mein 'Who's' aur 'Whose' dekhke bhi confuse ho jata hoon!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut important pakda! 'Who's' = 'Who is' ya 'Who has' (contraction hai, apostrophe wala). 'Whose' = possession (bina apostrophe). 'Who's coming?' vs 'Whose book is this?' - dono bilkul alag hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh apostrophe (') dekh ke pehchan sakte hain - agar apostrophe hai toh 'who is/has', nahi hai toh 'kiska'!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aakhri fark suno - 'WHICH' use hota hai jab OPTIONS/CHOICES limited/known ho. 'WHAT' use hota hai jab choices open/unlimited ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Jaise dukaan mein sirf 2 shirts dikh rahi hain - 'WHICH shirt do you want, red or blue?' Lekin agar koi limit nahi hai - 'WHAT do you want to eat?' (kuch bhi ho sakta hai).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh limited options = which, unlimited/open questions = what. Samajh gaya sir!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Who did you / (B) invite to the / (C) farewell party yesterday / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Shortening trick: 'You invited (who/whom)' - 'You invited him' fit hota hai, isliye Objective 'WHOM' sahi hai, na ki 'Who'. Correct: 'Whom did you invite'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) I do not know / (B) whose going to / (C) win the match tonight / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Yahan matlab 'who is going' hai, isliye contraction 'Who's' chahiye, possessive 'Whose' nahi. Correct: 'who's going to'.

quiz_payload.question: Choose the correctly formed sentence when the speaker is holding only two pens and asking the listener to choose:

options.text: What pen do you want, blue or black?
Which pen do you want, blue or black?
Who pen do you want, blue or black?
Whom pen do you want, blue or black?

quiz_payload.explanation: Jab options limited/known hon (yahan sirf 2 pens - blue ya black), tab 'Which' use hota hai, 'What' nahi.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Who/Whom ka boss ban gaye tum! Ab dekhते hain wahi words dobara - lekin is baar sentences JODNE (connect) ke liye - Relative Pronouns.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, in do sentences ko jodo: 'This is the boy.' + 'The boy won the race.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'This is the boy AND he won the race'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Achha attempt! Better/formal way: 'This is the boy WHO won the race.' Yahan 'who' do sentences ko JOD raha hai AND ek pronoun ki tarah 'boy' ko bhi replace kar raha hai - isliye ye RELATIVE Pronoun hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh matlab ye pronoun bhi hai aur conjunction (joड़ne wala) bhi - double kaam kar raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab relative pronoun mein bhi wahi WHO/WHOM ka rule chalega - PERSON ke liye 'who' (subject) aur 'whom' (object) use hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'The man WHOM I met yesterday is a doctor' - yahan 'whom' object hai kyunki 'I met him' fit ho raha hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Perfect application! Aur 'whose' relative pronoun ke roop mein possession dikhata hai, jaise 'The boy WHOSE bicycle was stolen cried a lot' - yahan bicycle boy ki thi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh insaan (person) ke liye who/whom/whose fix hai - cheez (things) ke liye kya use hoga sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Cheezon/animals ke liye 'WHICH' aur 'THAT' use hote hain. Lekin inme ek deep exam-level fark hai - COMMA ka role samjho. 'WHICH' comma ke saath aata hai (extra info), 'THAT' bina comma ke (zaroori info).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'My car, WHICH is red, is fast' - comma wala 'which' clause hataoge toh bhi sentence complete rahega (extra/non-essential info). Lekin 'The car THAT is parked outside is mine' - 'that' clause zaroori hai, hataoge toh sentence ka matlab hi kho jayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh comma ke saath 'which' = extra jaankari, bina comma 'that' = zaroori jaankari. Bahut fine difference hai sir ye toh!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aur important fact - 'THAT' (as Object) ko sentence se HATA bhi sakte hain, meaning wahi rahega. 'The book (that) I bought is nice' - dono sahi hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir toh 'which/who' ko bhi hata sakte hain kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Nahi! Jab relative pronoun SUBJECT ho (verb se pehle) tab kabhi hata nahi sakte. 'The man WHO called you is my uncle' - 'who' yahan subject hai, isse hataoge toh sentence hi tut jayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh sirf OBJECT wale 'that' ko drop kar sakte hain, subject wale kabhi nahi - clear ho gaya sir!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The candidate / (B) who the company selected / (C) was interviewed by three panels / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Shortening trick: 'the company selected (who/whom)' - 'the company selected him' fit ho raha hai, isliye Objective 'WHOM' sahi hai. Correct: 'whom the company selected'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The Taj Mahal / (B) that is located in Agra / (C) attracts millions of tourists every year / (D) No error

options.text: attracts millions of tourists every year

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Taj Mahal' ek unique/specific proper noun hai jiske baare mein extra (non-essential) info di ja rahi hai, isliye comma ke saath 'WHICH' use hoga, 'that' nahi. Correct: 'which is located in Agra,'.

quiz_payload.question: Which sentence correctly omits the relative pronoun?

options.text: The teacher called was very strict.
The teacher I met yesterday was very strict.
The teacher called me was very strict.
The teacher scolded students was very strict.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'The teacher (whom) I met yesterday' - yahan relative pronoun OBJECT position mein hai, isliye drop kar sakte hain. Options A, C, D mein relative pronoun SUBJECT position mein tha, jise drop nahi kar sakte - wo sentences galat hain.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Which/That ka comma-trick pakad liya tumne! Ab chalte hain 'each, either, neither' jaise Indefinite Pronouns ki taraf.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, gaon mein mela lag raha hai, aur tumhe pata nahi kaun aaya - tum bologe 'KOI toh aaya hai andar'. English mein?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'Someone has come inside'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! 'Someone' - yahan specific naam nahi bataya, DEFINITE nahi hai kaun hai. Isiliye some, any, no, every ke compounds (someone, anybody, nothing, everyone) ko INDEFINITE Pronoun kehte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'each, either, neither, none, all, few, many' bhi isi family mein aayenge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab strict rule yaad karo: EACH, EITHER, NEITHER - ye teeno hamesha SINGULAR verb aur SINGULAR pronoun lete hain, chahe unke saath 'of' + plural noun kyun na ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir example dijiye, samajhna hai achhe se!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'EACH of the students HAS submitted HIS assignment' - dhyan do, 'students' plural hai lekin verb 'has' aur pronoun 'his' singular hai, kyunki 'Each' asli subject hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh 'of the students' ko ignore karke 'Each' pe focus karna hai - ye toh bahut common trap lagta hai exam mein!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Aisa hi rule 'Some/Any/No/Every + one/body/thing' compounds pe bhi lagta hai - Everyone, Everybody, Everything, Someone, Anybody, Nothing - sab SINGULAR maane jaate hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye toh humne pichhle module mein 'everyone...their' wale trap mein dekha tha!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi yaad rakha! Yehi connection hai - saare indefinite pronoun jo 'one/body/thing' se khatam hote hain, wo singular hote hain: 'Everybody IS ready', 'Nothing HAS happened', 'Someone IS calling'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh ek pattern se saari indefinite pronoun family ki singular rule yaad ho gayi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab sabse professor-level trap - 'NONE'. Ye word 'no one' se banta hai, isliye traditionally SINGULAR hota hai. Lekin jab 'None of + plural noun' ho, tab modern usage mein PLURAL bhi chalta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye toh double confusion hai - kabhi singular kabhi plural?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exam ka safe rule: agar 'none' matlab 'not a single one' (ek bhi nahi) ho, toh singular use karo - 'None of the boys HAS come'. Agar matlab 'not any' (koi nahi, general) ho, toh plural bhi accept hota hai - 'None of them ARE here'. BPSC/SBI PO mein SINGULAR wala option zyada safe maana jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh agar dono options diye ho quiz mein, singular wala choose karunga - noted sir!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Either of the two roads / (B) lead to the / (C) railway station from here / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Either' hamesha singular verb leta hai, 'two roads' ko ignore karo. Correct: 'leads to the'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Nothing except lies / (B) come out of / (C) his mouth these days / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Nothing' ek indefinite pronoun hai jo hamesha SINGULAR verb leta hai. 'Except lies' ek phrase hai jo ignore hoga. Correct: 'comes out of'.

quiz_payload.question: Choose the most grammatically preferred (traditional/exam-safe) sentence:

options.text: None of the students has completed their homework.
None of the students have completed their homework.
None of the students has completed his homework.
None of the students having completed his homework.

quiz_payload.explanation: Exam-safe traditional rule: 'None' = 'not one', isliye singular verb 'has' aur singular pronoun 'his' dono match karke aana chahiye for full grammatical consistency, jo option C mein hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Each/Either/Neither/None ka singular rule pakka ho gaya! Ab dekhте hain ek nayi tarah ki galti - jab pronoun ka matlab hi unclear ho jaaye.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju suno ye sentence: 'Ravi told Suresh that HE had passed the exam.' Batao, 'HE' kaun hai - Ravi ya Suresh?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir... pata nahi, dono ho sakte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly yehi problem hai! Jab pronoun ka Antecedent CLEAR na ho (do options ho sakte hon), use 'AMBIGUOUS REFERENCE' error kehte hain - ye SBI PO/high level exams ka favorite hidden error hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Ye toh sabse tricky lag raha hai, kyunki sentence dekhne mein bilkul sahi lagta hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi observe kiya, dikhne mein bilkul theek lagta hai isliye khatarnak hai! Aisi hi galti hoti hai jab 'THIS/THAT/IT' kisi POORE IDEA ya PARAGRAPH ko refer karta hai, kisi specific noun ko nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'He failed the exam and got scolded by his father. THIS made him work harder.' - yahan 'This' kis specific noun ko refer kar raha hai? Kisi ek word ko nahi, PURE IDEA ko - ye vague/unclear reference hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, toh 'this/that/it' agar kisi single clear noun ki jagah nahi le raha, poore sentence ka matlab hi le raha hai, toh wo error hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab suno 'IT' ka ek bilkul alag, special use bhi hota hai - mausam, waqt aur distance batane mein. 'IT is raining', 'IT is 5 O'clock', 'IT is 10 km from here'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir yahan 'IT' kisko refer kar raha hai? Koi antecedent toh nahi dikh raha!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda - yahan 'IT' KISI KO refer NAHI karta, ye sirf ek 'Dummy Subject' ya 'Expletive IT' hai jo sirf grammatical structure poora karne ke liye lagaya jaata hai. Isko koi Antecedent dhoondhne ki zaroorat nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh 'It' ka special VIP use bhi hai jahan koi Antecedent rule follow nahi hota - exception yaad rakh liya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Aakhri type dekho - jab 'WHICH' kisi poore preceding clause ko refer kare, informal mein chalta hai but formal/exam grammar isse bhi error maanta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Example dijiye sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'He did not attend the meeting, WHICH surprised everyone.' - Yahan 'which' 'meeting' ko refer nahi kar raha, balki 'he not attending' wale poore idea ko refer kar raha hai. Formal English mein isse improve karke likhte hain: 'His absence from the meeting surprised everyone.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, toh ye subtle error hai jo direct dikhta bhi nahi - officer level exam isi liye tough hota hai!

quiz_payload.question: Identify the type of error in: 'Rahul told his father that he had won the scholarship.'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'He' Rahul ko refer kar raha hai ya uske father ko - dono possible hain, isliye ye Ambiguous Reference error hai. Correction ke liye direct speech ya name repeat karna padega: 'Rahul told his father, "I have won the scholarship."'

quiz_payload.question: In the sentence 'It is very hot today', what is the grammatical role of 'It'?

options.text: Personal Pronoun referring to the weather

quiz_payload.explanation: Weather, time, aur distance batane mein 'It' sirf ek grammatical placeholder (Dummy Subject/Expletive) hota hai - iska koi real antecedent nahi hota.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) The train arrived late / (B) which upset all / (C) the passengers waiting at the station / (D) No error

options.text: the passengers waiting at the station

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Which' yahan pure clause 'the train arrived late' ko refer kar raha hai, na ki kisi specific noun ko - ye formal grammar mein broad/vague reference error maana jaata hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Hidden errors ab tumse chhup nahi sakte! Aakhri module - special pronoun 'ONE' - jo bahut hi formal writing mein use hota hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, kabhi newspaper ya formal speech mein suna hai - 'ONE must always speak the truth'? Yahan 'One' kisko refer kar raha hai?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'One' matlab koi ek specific insaan?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Nahi Raju, yahan 'ONE' matlab GENERAL/ANY PERSON hai, sabke liye ek general statement - jaise Hindi mein 'insaan ko hamesha sach bolna chahiye'. Ye highly FORMAL writing mein use hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh ye 'One' bhi ek pronoun hai jo koi specific naam ki jagah general baat karta hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ab officer-level trap: agar sentence 'One' se start kiya hai, toh usi sentence mein aage bhi 'ONE/ONE'S/ONESELF' hi consistently use karna hoga - beech mein 'he/his' switch nahi kar sakte.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab sir 'One should always respect HIS parents' galat hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda! Formal British rule: 'One should always respect ONE'S parents' - consistency maintain karni hai, 'One' se 'his' pe kabhi switch nahi karna, chahe ye American English mein thoda accept ho jaaye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'One' start kiya matlab poore sentence mein 'One' ka hi family use karna hai - noted sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab pura family yaad karo - 'One' ka Possessive form hai 'ONE'S' (apostrophe-s ke saath), aur Reflexive form hai 'ONESELF' - jaise 'himself/herself' tha, waise hi 'oneself'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'One should not deceive ONESELF' - yahan 'oneself' reflexive hai, khud ko dhoka?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi! Aur remember - 'One's' mein apostrophe LAGTA hai (possessive adjective jaisa), lekin baaki possessive pronouns (his, hers, its, ours, theirs) mein apostrophe NAHI lagta. 'One's' ek exception hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh 'One's' hi ek aisa possessive hai jisme apostrophe lagta hai, baaki sab mein nahi - special case yaad rakhunga!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Aakhri aur bahut hi high-level trap: 'ONE OF THE + plural noun + WHO/THAT + verb'. Yahan verb PLURAL aayega, kyunki 'who/that' plural noun ko refer kar raha hai, 'one' ko nahi!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? 'One' toh singular hai sir, phir verb plural kaise?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahi toh sabse bada trap hai! 'He is ONE OF THE STUDENTS WHO HAVE passed' - 'who' yahan 'students' (plural, saare pass hue students mein se) ko refer kar raha hai, isliye 'have' plural aayega, na ki 'has'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wah sir, ye toh bahut khatarnak trap hai - main toh 'has' hi likhta har baar!

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) One should always / (B) try to complete / (C) his duty honestly / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Sentence 'One' se start hua hai, isliye consistency maintain karte hue 'his' ki jagah 'one's' aana chahiye. Correct: 'one's duty honestly'.

quiz_payload.question: Find the error (SBI PO Style): (A) Ramesh is one of / (B) the best students / (C) who has ever joined this college / (D) No error

options.text: who has ever joined this college

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Who' yahan 'students' (plural) ko refer kar raha hai, isliye plural verb aayega. Correct: 'who have ever joined this college'.

quiz_payload.question: Choose the correctly written sentence:

options.text: One must always believe in oneself.
One must always believe in himself.
One must always believe in ones self.
One must always believe in one self.

quiz_payload.explanation: Reflexive form of 'One' hai 'ONESELF' (ek hi word mein, no space, no apostrophe). 'Himself' consistency todta hai, aur 'ones self'/'one self' galat spelling forms hain.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Saare 12 modules clear! Ab officer level ki final revision aur master quiz baaki hai - chalo pura chapter ek baar mein revise karte hain!

revision_points.point: Statement I: After a preposition, always use Objective case ('between you and me'). Statement II: After 'than/as', use the case that fits the hidden verb ('taller than I am'). Both statements are CORRECT and frequently combined in multi-statement BPSC/SBI PO questions.

Statement I: Collective nouns (team, jury, family) take singular pronoun when acting as one unit. Statement II: Indefinite pronouns (everyone, each, everybody) always take singular pronoun (his/her). Both statements are CORRECT - this combination is a BPSC favorite trap.

Statement I: 'Myself' can replace 'I/me' as a subject/object in any sentence. Statement II: 'Himself' after a noun for emphasis is called an Intensive Pronoun. Statement I is INCORRECT (reflexive needs a matching subject first); Statement II is CORRECT.

Statement I: 'Each other' is used for two persons, 'one another' for more than two. Statement II: 'Which' takes a comma for non-essential info, 'that' never takes a comma. Both statements are CORRECT.

Statement I: A sentence starting with 'One' must consistently use 'one's/oneself', never 'his/himself'. Statement II: 'None' traditionally takes a singular verb, meaning 'not a single one'. Both statements are CORRECT and are Officer-level favorites.

quiz_payload.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Pronoun usage:
Statement I: In the sentence 'Neither of the answers are correct', the verb should be singular ('is') because 'Neither' is grammatically singular.
Statement II: In the sentence 'Each of the players have their own kit', the verb should be singular ('has') because 'Each' is grammatically singular.
Statement III: In 'Ravi is one of the boys who has topped the exam', the verb 'has' is correct because 'one' controls the verb.
Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?

options.text: Statements I and II are correct
Statements I, II and III are correct

quiz_payload.explanation: Statement I is CORRECT: 'Neither' is always singular, so 'is correct' is right, not 'are correct'. Statement II is CORRECT: 'Each' is always singular, so verb should be 'has', not 'have' (also pronoun should be 'his', not 'their'). Statement III is INCORRECT: In 'one of the boys WHO...', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'boys' (plural), so the verb must be 'have', not 'has'. Hence only I and II are correct - Option B.
